# Mission 1

## Trial Synthesis

From all 3 trials, only the straight-line test closely matched expectations, while the turns consistently showed less rotation than intended. The biggest difference happened in trial 2, where the robot only made a heading change of 0.7630 rad where it was predicted to do 3.14 rad. This is most likely a command issue or duration issue where a safety node lowered the speed or time duration of the original command. We can look at the timestamps on student_cmd_vel and see if it had any changes in command values.

## Hallway Analysis

Sudden turns or abrupt straight driving could scare pedestrians because the robot's path to an outsider isn't obvious. Lowering the turn rate will make the motion smoother and more predictable. Downside being a maneuver will take longer. We can use lidar to track and detect people and objects to limit speed when close to things or people for safety, then ramp it up when clear.
